title: Slėptuvės Dubysos g. 39 atnaujinimo ir modernizavimo techninio darbo projekto parengimo ir projekto vykdymo priežiūros paslaugos.

title: Ireland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Web applications maintenance support and Development Services
description: Teagasc is seeking tenders for the maintenance, support and ongoing development of web applications software. Teagasc has a number of bespoke systems that have been developed by third party suppliers. These systems are key systems used by Teagasc in the supply of its services to its clients and the general public. The technology used is primarily from the Microsoft stack. These Web Applications are public facing business applications hosted by Teagasc on premises in its Demilitarized Zone, along with some associated services. This tender competition is divided into three lots. Services required across all Lots as follows: 1. Support the Web Applications at a system level, resolving any bugs or issues with the software and ensuring its smooth day to day operation and availability 2. Supply development services for an ongoing programme of development for the software. 3. Support and maintenance to cover the applications listed in both the existing test and production environments and any future project environments.

title: Request for Offers for the provision of Cleaning Services for the Embassy of Canada to Lebanon, in Beirut
description: The cleaning services must be delivered at The Canadian Embassy to Lebanon, in Beirut. The work includes the provision of routine and periodic cleaning services, as well as any additional cleaning required to meet operational needs. Services must be provided in accordance with the specifications outlined in this Statement of Work and must support a clean, safe, and professional environment at all times while not interfering with the daily operations or activities of the building’s occupants, clients, or visitors. The Canadian Embassy in Beirut, Lebanon is in Spark Tower Bldg, 2415 Sin El Fil, Beirut, Lebanon, a business centre comprising 18 Floors. The total surface area occupied by the embassy is of 3550 m2 and comprises: part of the Ground Floor, the Fourteenth floor, the Fifteenth floor, the Sixteenth floor, the Mezzanine in the Sixteenth floor, the Seventeenth floor, parking spaces, storage rooms, guards and drivers’ rooms. While the majority of the work will be located at the Chancery Building of the Embassy located in Sin El Fil, cleaning staff may be called upon to provide similar work at the Official Residence of the Ambassador or at the apartments of the Embassy’s diplomatic staff in Ashrafieh, or at any other venue as required by the Embassy of Canada. Periodical cleaning of the exterior windows of staff quarters may be required and will be paid following an offer and at the submission of an invoice. The pricing will be quoted per occurrences and must be approved by the contracting authority before work starts.

description: Keski-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjousta jätehuolto- ja viemäröintipalveluista. Hankinta on jaettu seuraaviin osa-alueisiin: osa 1 Yhdyskuntajätteet osa 2 Tietoturvajätteet osa 3 Vaaralliset ja terveydenhuollon erityisjätteet osa 4 Loka- ja rasvanerotuskaivot Tarjouksen voi antaa yhdestä tai useammasta osa-alueesta, mutta osa-alueen sisällä on tarjottava jokaiseen kysyttyyn kohtaan. title: Kotiin vietävät ateriapalvelut
description: Kotiin vietävät ateriapalvelut Keski-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjousta kotiin vietävistä ateriapalveluista seuraavien Keski-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen kuntien alueella: Halsua, Kannus, Kokkola, Lestijärvi, Perho, Toholampi ja Veteli. Sopimus on määräaikainen ja voimassa kaksi (2) vuotta sopimuksen alkamisesta. Tilaajalla on lisäksi oikeus kahteen (2) erikseen päätettävään yhden (1) vuoden optiokauteen. Sopimuksen arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 1.2.2027. Hankinnan kohteena on kylmänä toimitettavat kotiateriat Keski-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen asiakkaille. Kyseessä on sosiaalihuoltolain (1301/2014) 19 §:n mukainen tukipalvelu. Kotihoidon asiakkaat ovat pääsääntöisesti ikääntyneitä, joilla on usein alentunut fyysinen toimintakyky ja/tai muistin alenema ja jotka vielä pärjäävät itsenäisesti omassa tutussa elinympäristössään mm. ateriapalvelujen avulla. Asiakkaina on myös rintamaveteraaneja ja sotainvalideja sekä omaishoidontuen piirissä olevia asiakkaita. Hankittava palvelu sisältää aterioiden valmistuksen, kuljetuksen ja kaiken muun, mitä kyseiseen prosessiin liittyy. Hankittava palvelun määrä voi vaihdella sopimuskaudella. Sopimus ei sisällä Tilaajalle määräostovelvoitetta. Hankinnan kohde on määritelty tarkemmin tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä.,

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Sanierung Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad in D-98646 Hildburghausen - Generalplanung nach §§ 34, 51, 55 HOAI 2021 sowie Besondere Leistungen
description: Das Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad in Hildburghausen ist seit der Errichtung und Einweihung im Jahr 2000 ein zentraler und wichtiger Bestandteil der regionalen Infrastruktur, da es eine unverzichtbare Funktion in den Bereichen Sport, Bildung, Freizeit und Gesundheit erfüllt. Im Besonderen ist hier die Funktion für die Schwimmausbildung im Rahmen des Schulschwimmens für den kompletten Landkreises Hildburghausen zu nennen. Als Ganzjahresbad mit einer Kombination aus Hallen- und Freibadbereich sichert es die Schwimmausbildung für Schulen und Vereine in der Region und dient als wichtige Trainingsstätte für den lokalen Sport. Die große Badelandschaft mit 25 m-Bahnen und Sprungturm ist essenziell für die allgemeine Fitness und das sportliche Training. Darüber hinaus ist das Bad ein beliebtes regionales Ausflugsziel und ein wichtiger sozialer Treffpunkt. Mit Attraktionen wie der 50 m-Riesenrutsche, einem Spaßbecken mit Massagedüsen und einem separaten Kinderplanschbecken bietet es einen wetterunabhängigen Anziehungspunkt für Familien und Erholungssuchende aus dem gesamten Landkreis. Ergänzt wird dieses Angebot durch eine Saunalandschaft, die den Aspekt Wellness und Gesundheitsförderung abdeckt. Zusammenfassend lässt sich sagen, dass das Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad weit über die Funktion eines einfachen Schwimmbades hinausgeht: Es steigert die Lebensqualität der Bürger und bildet eine tragende Säule der Freizeit- und Sportinfrastruktur in Hildburghausen und Süddthüringen. Während die lange diskutierte und komplexe Sanierung des Freibadbereiches im Jahr 2024 abgeschlossen werden konnte, steht nun die umfassende Ertüchtigung der Schwimmhalle selbst an. Trotz einer kleineren Sanierung der Halle im Jahr 2018 sind die technischen Anlagen, die Gebäudehülle und die Innenbereiche nach über zwei Jahrzehnten intensiver Nutzung in einem Zustand, der eine Generalüberholung notwendig macht. Diese Sanierung muss deutlich über kosmetische Reparaturen hinausgehen und die technische, energetische und gestalterische Modernisierung der gesamten Halle sowie der angeschlossenen Saunalandschaft umfassen. Ziel ist es, den Energieverbrauch langfristig zu senken und das Bad zukunftsfähig zu machen. Die Sanierung des Werra Sport- und Freizeitbades ist eine komplexe und anspruchsvolle Planungsaufgabe, für die ein kompetentes Planerteam gesucht wird. Die Brutto-Grundfläche des Gebäudes (BGF) beträgt ca. 3.600 m2. Die Wasserfläche umfasst ca. 480 m2. Für die geplante Maßnahme werden Baukosten von ca. 4,0 Mio Euro (Brutto, KG 300 und 400) veranschlagt.

Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), located in Indian Head, Maryland, intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) purchase order using Simplified Acquisition Procedures for Body, Retainer, and Gasket parts. This RFQ incorporates all provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) DPN 20260507. Price: Quotes must include all applicable costs, including shipping and handling. title: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit
description: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, (USACE) Pittsburgh District has a requirement for the retrofitting of existing hydraulic structures within an active navigation lock. The Prime Contractor must be capable of executing complex in-the-wet construction, specifically: The John P. Murtha Floating Mooring Bitt Retrofit consists of the installation of Government furnished Floating Mooring Bitts into Contractor fabricated embedded frame on the existing River Chamber Middle Wall. In-the-wet construction methods are required. Design, fabrication, and installation of two dewatering boxes are required for installation of the Floating Mooring Bitts. Removal or alterations to existing work in such a manner as to prevent injury or damage to any portions of the existing work which remain. Repair or replace portions of existing work which have been altered during construction operations to match existing or adjoining work, as approved by the Contracting Officer. At the completion of operations, existing work must be in a condition equal to or better than that which existed before new work started. To achieve this Requirement the Contractor must: a. Floating Plant Operations: Providing, operating, and mooring a fully compliant floating plant (crane/deck barge and push boat) in an active river chamber in accordance with EM 385-1-1. b. Dewatering Box (Cofferdam): Fabricating, installing, and sealing structural steel dewatering boxes against lock monoliths for a strict maximum duration of 90 days. c. Heavy Demolition and Concrete Work: Executing concrete wire-sawing, core drilling, and demolition of existing lock wall recesses, followed by cast-in-place concrete integration. d. Structural Steel and Mooring Bitts: Fabricating heavy steel embedded anchorage frames, and salvaging/installing Government-Furnished Floating Mooring Bitts. e. Commercial Diving: Providing certified commercial dive teams to support underwater inspection, rigging, and cofferdam sealing. The work shall be completed within 730 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed. This acquisition will be procured as an Unrestricted Full and Open Solicitation. The resulting award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Construction Contract. All responsible Bidders are encouraged to participate. The Invitation for Bid (IFB) will be issued on or about 15 September 2026, online through Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) which posts the opportunity to SAM.gov; therefore, requests for hardcopies of the solicitation will not be honored. .The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) for this procurement is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the small business size standard is $45Million.In order to submit a Bid on this project, your company must-1) Be registered in System for Award Management (SAM) and maintain an active registration status. 2) Be registered in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) for the Solicitation Module with the PROPOSAL MANAGER role. System for Award Management (SAM) Registration. Registering in SAM.gov includes both entity validation and entity registration. To register in SAM: a. Navigate to SAM.gov b. Select Sign-In (top right) c. Select Create an Account then Follow the Instructions. d. After Account is Set-up, Select Sign In. e. Under the Entity Management widget, Select Get Started button. f. title: Marine Corps Acquisition Exchange (MCAX) Hosted by Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC), Headquarters Marine Corps Installations & Logistics (HQMC I&L), and Including Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) Information Tec
description: When: Thursday, 19 November 2026, 9:30 a.m. EST. The event will last approximately four hours. Where: Join us in person or virtually via Microsoft Teams. During registration, industry partners will be asked to indicate their preferred method of attendance (in person or virtual). Because venue capacity is limited, requesting in-person attendance does not guarantee an in-person invitation. In-person attendance will be limited to two representatives per entity. Invitations will generally be issued in registration order, subject to venue capacity and Government discretion, including consideration for first-time attendees. After registration closes, confirmed in-person attendees and virtual participants will receive the appropriate access information by email. Registration Closes: 5 Nov 2026 Ready to join us? Register using the link below. Please copy and paste the link into your browser rather than attempting to access it directly through SAM.gov: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/Cx4WtRHSKa If you experience issues with the registration link, please contact us at: SMB_PAE_MC_CTIndustry@usmc.mil One quick favor before you hit submit: Please double-check your email address and telephone number. Your invitation and event information will be sent using the contact information you provide during registration. An incorrect email address means we will not be able to get your invitation to you. In the event of unforeseen technical issues, the virtual session may be cancelled. If that happens, presentation materials will be provided to registered attendees following the event. BACKGROUND Let�s Talk About What�s Next. Good acquisition starts with communication. Not just when a solicitation hits SAM.gov. Not just when proposals are due. And certainly not only after we already know exactly what we want to buy. Sometimes the most valuable conversation happens much earlier. On 19 November 2026, Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC) and Headquarters Marine Corps Installations & Logistics (HQMC I&L) invite industry to join us for our next quarterly Marine Corps Acquisition Exchange (MCAX). Together with the Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) Information Technology Contracting Center (ITCC) and other Marine Corps acquisition and requirements stakeholders, we want to give industry a clearer look at where we're headed�and an opportunity to talk with the people helping us get there. The 19 November MCAX will provide industry with visibility into anticipated contracting opportunities across participating Marine Corps organizations, while creating dedicated time for questions and direct Government�Industry engagement. What are we looking for? Ideas. Capabilities. Competition. Innovation. And, most importantly, meaningful dialogue with industry partners who understand that supporting the Marine Corps begins with understanding the mission. Our senior leaders, Capability Portfolio Managers, acquisition professionals, PAE MC Rapid Capability Cell (RCC) representatives, and Small Business experts will share information about emerging requirements, acquisition priorities, and anticipated contracting opportunities across the Marine Corps enterprise. And we don't want the conversation to go only one way. MCAX is also our opportunity to hear from you. What are you seeing in the marketplace? Where is technology moving? What capabilities already exist that we should know about? And where can better communication between Government and Industry help us find smarter ways to meet the needs of the warfighter? That exchange matters. Because when Government better understands what industry can deliver�and industry better understands where the Marine Corps is going�we can have better conversations about how to get there. Whether you've supported the Marine Corps for decades, you're an innovative small business looking for your first opportunity, or you're somewhere in between, you're invited to be part of that conversation. Come hear what we're working on. Ask questions. Engage with the people behind the requirements. And gain a clearer understanding of where your capabilities may align with what comes next. EVENT FORMAT We know your time is valuable. That's why we're continuing to focus MCAX on the information and engagement that industry has told us matters most. The approximately four-hour live event is anticipated to include: Briefs from leaders in Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC), Headquarters Marine Corps, Installations & Logistics (HQMC I&L), Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS), PAE MC Cyber Technology Office, PAE MC RCC, and the Combat Development & Integration (CD&I) Capability Portfolio Managers (CPMs) Contract Opportunity Briefs from PAE MC, HQMC I&L and PAE MS Information Technology Contracting Center (ITCC) Industry Q&A We will continue streamlining formal presentations wherever possible so there is more time for meaningful engagement between Industry and Government. And because showing up prepared makes for a better conversation, we're giving you a head start. Before MCAX, take some time to explore the PAE MC Industry Portal at: https://www.pae.marines.mil/industry-portal/ The portal is designed to help industry learn more about PAE MC, our mission, and how to engage with us before the conversation begins. Have a capability we should know about? Industry partners are encouraged to submit capability briefs or white papers through the Industry Portal before the event. Sharing that information in advance gives our team an opportunity to better understand what you bring to the table and where your capabilities may connect with Marine Corps needs. A preview of selected contracting opportunities associated with the 19 November MCAX will also be added to this notice as soon as it becomes available. Industry partners are encouraged to check this notice periodically for updates prior to the event, review the opportunities in advance, and come ready to engage. HQMC I&L opportunities will be released to industry within five business days following the event through a separate SAM.gov announcement. One Mission. Many Opportunities. One Conversation Worth Having. We hope you'll join us on 19 November.

title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

title: Y1DA--VISN 2 EHRM Industry Day
description: Construction Industry Day Introduction In accordance with FAR Companion (FC) 10.001(c), this notice is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), nor will the VA pay for information requested. Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) will host an industry day event at the James J. Peters Department of Veterans Affairs VA Medical Center (VAMC), located at 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, NY 10468 for all businesses (including, but not limited to, general contractors, subcontractor trades, and material suppliers) interested in the upcoming Electronic Health Records Modernization (EHRM) Infrastructure Upgrades construction projects throughout VISN 2 (NY/NJ). The purpose of the Industry Day is to facilitate collaboration between the VA and general construction contractors and subcontractors of all business sizes who are interested in performing work in New York and New Jersey. This session is designed to give all interested contractors a clear understanding of the project s intent, performance expectations, and execution approach. This industry day will help the VA determine the method of procurement and type of socioeconomic set-aside, if any, highlight any industry concerns, gauge general contractor interest in the project, and perform a site walk to show key areas of the Bronx EHRM project. Six EHRM Infrastructure projects were solicited and awarded in FY26. Four of the six were designated as SDVOSB set-asides, and most of these projects received limited bids or proposals. In FY27, VISN 2 anticipates three projects, Bronx, Manhattan, and Northport, that are particularly large and complex, which may pose significant challenges for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) to execute independently due to their scale and technical requirements. As a result, the VA is considering broadening the competition beyond SDVOSBs, seeking participation from both small and/or large businesses that have the project experience, capabilities, and workforce necessary to fulfill the contract demands. This approach is critical to ensuring a robust competitive environment that accurately reflects market value and supports successful project delivery. EVENT INFORMATION The industry day will be held on Thursday, November 19th, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM ET. The meeting location will be Room 3D-22 in Building 100, located at 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, NY 10468. Contractors are required to pre-register for this event. See Administrative section below. Proposed Agenda: 1. Check-in (please arrive between 9 - 9:30 AM) 2. Introductions 3. Meet and Greet 4. Overview of the EHRM Program and Each Project 4. Site walk of the Bronx VAMC EHRM project 5. Lunch Break 6. Questions and answers session 7. Networking *A final agenda will most likely be posted to SAM.gov closer to the event date. PROJECT DESCRIPTIONS VISN 2 (New York/New Jersey) has five EHRM projects that are anticipated to be solicited and awarded in Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 and four in FY 2028. The five planned locations for FY27 are at the following VAMC s: Bronx, Canandaigua, Manhattan, Northport, and St. Albans. A description of each project is listed below. Bronx VAMC: The design modernizes the campus technology backbone and supporting building systems so the medical center can implement the VA EHRM platform while maintaining reliable clinical and facility operations. Work extends across the Main Hospital (Building 100) and multiple adjacent campus buildings and support facilities. A distinguishing feature is the construction of two new telecommunications towers. The towers expand communications capacity and require coordinated architectural, structural, civil, electrical, mechanical, and telecommunications design. The broader project also renovates and expands existing telecommunications and data center spaces and upgrades the supporting power, cooling, fiber, security, and life-safety infrastructure. Canandaigua VAMC: This project comprehensively upgrades the campus s fiber optic network and power distribution systems to meet EHRM design guide requirements, ensuring robust support for clinical and facility operations. The work encompasses fiber network enhancements with redundant routes to each IT closet and the main demarcation room, minimizing risk through parallel systems operation during transitions from legacy to new infrastructure. The project also includes expansion or relocation of telecommunications rooms, installation of 100 new IT outlets and 75 electrical outlets, and substantial improvements in power distribution and HVAC systems. Enhanced physical security is provided through secure data cabinets, protected fiber infrastructure, secured telecommunications rooms, and installation of lockable manhole covers for underground fiber pathways. In addition, hazardous material abatement activities will ensure that all upgraded spaces meet current safety and environmental standards. Manhattan VAMC: The design modernizes telecommunications and IT infrastructure throughout Buildings 1, 2, 3, and 6 and creates resilient power and cooling systems to support continuous healthcare operations and future technology demands. The project relocates the existing data center to renovated space and upgrades 53 telecommunications rooms and enclosures. The new data center functions as the campus telecommunications hub and is supported by redundant fiber pathways, dedicated year-round cooling, and 2N UPS and electrical distribution redundancy. These features distinguish the Manhattan project and increase the reliability of critical IT systems. Northport VAMC: This information will be provided in an update to this posting on SAM.gov. St. Albans VAMC: The EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades Project at St. Albans VA Medical Center in Queens, NY, is a large-scale modernization effort designed to support the implementation of the VA s new EHRM system. The initiative involves major upgrades across multiple buildings, including the construction of a new data center and telecom tower, extensive electrical and mechanical improvements, and the installation of advanced technology infrastructure such as Cat 6A cabling and a fiber optic backbone, all guided by strict VA standards for compliance, safety, and scalability. Key challenges include managing hazardous materials like asbestos and lead-based paint, addressing spatial and technical constraints in existing telecom rooms, coordinating complex system upgrades within an active healthcare environment, and ensuring meticulous phasing to minimize disruptions. Additionally, the project must integrate diverse building systems, adhere to evolving standards, and provide future-proofing for anticipated growth, all of which add significant complexity to both the design and execution phases. *The following projects anticipated for award in FY28: Albany, Buffalo, Batavia and East Orange. Procurement Information The proposed projects will be a competitive firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-bid-build approach (final specifications and drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued as either request for proposals (RFP) in accordance with FAR part 15, considering technical and price factors or Invitation for Bids (IFBs) in accordance with FAR part 14, considering price only. The full acquisition strategy for this proposed project has not yet been developed and will be determined after the industry day and any additional market research is concluded. The targeted cost ranges of each project are listed below. Between $20 and $30 Million: Canandaigua and St. Albans Between $40 and $50 Million: Bronx and Manhattan Between $50 and $60 Million: Northport The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small business size standard of $45 million. Countermeasures That Work (CMTW) Updates
description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) maintains Countermeasures That Work, an evidence-based reference guide used by State Highway Safety Offices (SHSOs) and other stakeholders to identify effective behavioral traffic safety countermeasures. NHTSA is seeking contractor support to update the guide based on the latest available research, emerging countermeasures, and developments in highway safety. The purpose of this requirement is to update the current 12th edition of Countermeasures That Work and its electronic version (E-CMTW), resulting in the 13th edition. The contractor will conduct comprehensive literature searches, review and evaluate relevant research, and incorporate significant new findings, resources, and implementation considerations into approximately three to four program-area chapters annually. The final deliverable will include a consolidated Word document incorporating all updates made during the period of performance.

title: Countermeasures That Work (CMTW) Updates
description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) maintains Countermeasures That Work, an evidence-based reference guide used by State Highway Safety Offices (SHSOs) and other stakeholders to identify effective behavioral traffic safety countermeasures. NHTSA is seeking contractor support to update the guide based on the latest available research, emerging countermeasures, and developments in highway safety. The purpose of this requirement is to update the current 12th edition of Countermeasures That Work and its electronic version (E-CMTW), resulting in the 13th edition. The contractor will conduct comprehensive literature searches, review and evaluate relevant research, and incorporate significant new findings, resources, and implementation considerations into approximately three to four program-area chapters annually. The final deliverable will include a consolidated Word document incorporating all updates made during the period of performance.

When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. QUALITY ASSURANCE 4.1 Responsibility for Inspection - Unless otherwise specified in the contract/purchase order, the Contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein.

SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy�s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. If your company is NOT requesting the classified source code, please state "Not Applicable" or "N/A" for these fields. title: Germany – Construction work for school buildings – Heidacker 13 - Hamburger Schulhaus und Zweifeldhalle als GU-Leistung
description: Die GMH | Gebäudemanagement Hamburg GmbH ist ein städtisches Unternehmen, welches u.a. für über 50 allgemeinbildende Schulen im Süden Hamburgs (Wilhelmsburg und Harburg) sowie für Gebäude des Hochschul- und Kommunalbaus die Dienstleistungen des Baus, des Betriebes und der Bewirtschaftung wahrnimmt. --------------- Der Schulstandort Heidacker 13 in Hamburg-Eidelstedt soll zukunftsfähig ausgebaut werden. Auf dem Grundstück sind die folgenden Neubaumaßnahmen geplant: 1) Zubau Hamburger Schulhaus (angelehnt an das Hamburger Klassenhaus) und 2) Zubau Zweifeldhalle. Gegenstand der vorliegenden GU-Ausschreibung ist der Zubau des Hamburger Schulhauses in Anlehnung an das Hamburger Klassenhaus. Die Realisierung erfolgt über einen Generalunternehmer, der die LPH 5-8 erbringt und das Gebäude in vorgefertigter Bauweise erstellt. Das bestehende Schulgelände umfasst einen Gebäudebestand von 6 Gebäuden unterschiedlicher Gebäudeklassen inkl. einer bestehenden und an das Baufeld angrenzenden mobilen Klassenraumanlage. Letztere verbleibt bis zur Fertigstellung des Hamburger Schulhauses im Betrieb. Das Grundstück weist eine Gesamtfläche von ca. 20.861 m² auf. Für die Schule ist eine 5-Zügigkeit geplant. Im dreigeschossigen Gebäude, mit einer BGF in Höhe von ca. 2.019 m² und einer Mietfläche (NRF) in Höhe von ca. 1.729 m², werden im EG ein Foyer, eine Essenseinnahmefläche, eine Vitalküche für 300-600 VT, eine kleine Multifunktionsfläche und sonstige Nebenflächen vorgesehen. Im 1.OG werden 3 geschlossene Klassenräume, 2 geschlossene Lernstudios, 1 offene Multifunktionsfläche, 1 „Maker Hub“ mit Podcaststudio, 1 Bibliothek, 1 Teeküche, Garderobenflächen und sonstige Nebenflächen vorgesehen. Im 2.OG werden 3 geschlossene Klassenräume, 2 geschlossene Lernstudios, 1 offene Multifunktionsfläche, 1 Handarbeits-/ Handwerksfläche inkl. Lernstützpunkt, 1 Kunstatelier und sonstige Nebenflächen vorgesehen. --------------- Hier: GU-Leistung --------------- Schlüsselfertige Erstellung eines Neubaus

title: Germany – Photographic services – Bildbeurteilung und -bearbeitung für die eGK
description: Die Techniker Krankenkasse (TK) gibt gem. § 291 SGB V für jeden Versicherten eine elektronische Gesundheitskarte (eGK) aus. Die eGK dient als Nachweis zur Inanspruchnahme von Leistungen im Rahmen der vertragsärztlichen Versorgung und ist für Versicherte ab 15 Jahren grundsätzlich mit einem Bild des Karteninhabers auszustatten. Aus diesem Grund fordert die TK bei ihren Kunden ein Bild an. Die angeforderten Bilder können auf dem Postweg eingereicht oder online hochgeladen werden. Die bei der TK eingereichten Bilder werden, so diese nicht online hochgeladen wurden, im ersten Schritt von der TK digitalisiert. Die weitere Bildbeurteilung und -bearbeitung nimmt die TK nicht selbst vor, sondern beauftragt hierfür den Auftragnehmer (AN). Dieser prüft, beurteilt und bearbeitet die Fotos zu eGK-spezifikationskonformen Bildern für die Produktion der eGK.

title: Sweden – Ferry transport services – Färjeförbindelse på Ekeröleden
description: Ekerö kommun avser att upphandla färjeförbindelse på Ekeröleden för perioden 2027-07-01 till det datum förbifarten öppnar (planerat 2030). Förutsättningar Sedan 30 år tillbaka bedriver Ekerö kommun en färjeverksamhet som kopplar ihop Ekerö och söderorten i Botkyrka kommun för olika trafikslag. Ekerö kommun har avtal med Trafikverket avseende färjeverksamheten. Avtalet med Trafikverket upphör 2027-06-30 och kan inte förlängas ytterligare. År 2030 öppnas Förbifart E4, som skapar en snabbare förbindelse mellan Ekerö kommun och söderorten för bil- och busstrafik. Tidsvinsten som färjan ger idag kommer till största delen försvinna för de betalande kunderna om man kan åka till söderorten och Södertörn genom den nya tunneln. Både användningen och betalningsviljan bland användare kommer att minska rejält. Eftersom Ekeröledens affärsmodell bygger på användaravgifter kommer även en liten minskning av resandeunderlaget resultera i att intäkterna inte längre kan täcka kostnaderna. Avtalstid Avtalstiden är 2027-07-01 till och med 2031-06-30. Ekerö kommun har en uppsägningstid på tolv (12) månader och avtalet planeras att sägas upp när besked finns kring förbifartens slutgiltiga öppnande så att färjetrafiken enligt detta avtal upphör två (2) till (3) veckor efter öppnandet. Tidplan Ekerö kommun planerar att tilldela upphandlingen i december 2026.

title: Atpūtas un labsajūtas kompleksa būvniecība
description: Iepirkuma priekšmets ir būvdarbu veikšana saskaņā ar būvprojektu "Viesu nama, pirts un saimniecības ēkas būvniecība īpašumā "Mazveiti", Nīcas pagastā, Dienvidkurzemes novadā (būvprojekta izmaiņas)", būvprojekta rasējumiem, darbu apjomu sarakstiem, tehniskajām specifikācijām un citiem iepirkuma dokumentiem. Būvdarbu izpildītājam jāveic visi būvprojektā paredzētie darbi, nodrošinot objekta pilnīgu pabeigšanu un nodošanu ekspluatācijā atbilstoši Latvijas Republikas normatīvo aktu prasībām. Pretendentam jāparedz visi palīgdarbi, pagaidu darbi, materiāli, mehānismi, transports, darba aizsardzības pasākumi un citi resursi, kas nepieciešami kvalitatīvai un pilnīgai būvdarbu izpildei, pat ja tie nav atsevišķi norādīti darbu apjomu sarakstos. Pretendents ir pilnībā atbildīgs par būvdarbu organizēšanu un vadību, izmantoto materiālu, izstrādājumu un iekārtu atbilstību Latvijas Republikas normatīvo aktu prasībām, būvdarbu kvalitāti un izpildes termiņu ievērošanu, būvniecības procesa dokumentācijas sagatavošanu un uzturēšanu, būvlaukuma uzturēšanu kārtībā un objekta sakārtošanu pēc būvdarbu pabeigšanas. Visiem materiāliem, izstrādājumiem un iekārtām jābūt jauniem, nelietotiem, sertificētiem un atbilstošiem Latvijas Republikā spēkā esošo normatīvo aktu prasībām. Ja būvdarbu izpildes laikā tiek konstatēta nepieciešamība veikt tehnoloģiski nepieciešamus darbus, kas nav atsevišķi uzskaitīti darbu apjomu sarakstos, bet ir nepieciešami būvprojekta pilnīgai realizācijai un būves nodošanai ekspluatācijā, pretendents šādus darbus paredz savā finanšu piedāvājumā, izņemot gadījumus, kad normatīvie akti nosaka citu kārtību papildu darbu veikšanai. Pretendentam ir tiesības iesniegt alternatīvu tehnisko risinājumu, ja tas uzskata, ka būvprojektā paredzētos darbus iespējams realizēt citā tehnoloģiskā secībā vai izmantojot citus tehniskos risinājumus, kas nodrošina zemākas būvniecības izmaksas, nesamazinot būvdarbu kvalitāti, funkcionalitāti, drošību, ilgmūžību un ekspluatācijas īpašības. Alternatīvajam risinājumam pilnībā jāatbilst spēkā esošo normatīvo aktu prasībām un jānodrošina būves nodošana ekspluatācijā normatīvajos aktos noteiktajā kārtībā. Pasūtītājs patur tiesības izvērtēt iesniegto alternatīvo risinājumu un pieņemt vai noraidīt to, ja tas neatbilst iepirkuma prasībām, būvprojekta mērķim vai spēkā esošo normatīvo aktu prasībām. Pretendentam jābūt reģistrētam Latvijas Republikas Būvkomersantu reģistrā. Pretendentam pēdējo 10 (desmit) gadu laikā jābūt sekmīgi izpildītiem vismaz diviem būvdarbu līgumiem, kuru priekšmets ir ēku jaunbūve, pārbūve vai atjaunošana un kuru raksturs, apjoms un sarežģītība ir līdzvērtīga šī iepirkuma priekšmetam. Pretendentam jānodrošina sertificēts būvdarbu vadītājs un citi normatīvajos aktos paredzētie būvspeciālisti, kuriem ir spēkā esoši profesionālās darbības sertifikāti attiecīgajā būvniecības jomā. Piedāvājumiem jābūt apliecinātiem ar e- parakstu.

title: Rulle- og aktivitetspark ved Gimle skule
description: Fyresdal kommune skal etablere ein rulle- og aktivitetspark ved Gimle skule. Anskaffinga blir gjennomført som ein samspelsentreprise i to fasar. Fase 1 omfattar vidareutvikling av forstudiet, nødvendige tekniske undersøkingar, forprosjekt, medverknad, kostnadskalkyle, finansieringsgrunnlag og målpris. Fase 2 er ein opsjon og omfattar detaljprosjektering og bygging som totalentreprise etter NS 8407. Det rettleiande konseptet omfattar eit aktivitetsområde på om lag 3 600 m² med plasstøypt betongskatepark på om lag 850 til 900 m², pumptrack, trampolineområde, calisthenics, bordtennis, gapahuk, møteplassar, landskap, gangareal og nødvendige grunn- og dreneringsarbeid. Heile programmet skal utviklast og prisast i fase 1. Kommunen kan bruke nærmare angitte fradragsopsjonar dersom finansieringa gjer dette nødvendig.

title: Netherlands – Energy and related services – Programmateam Waarm Fryslân
description: De aanleiding voor deze opdracht is dat de warmtetransitie in Fryslân relatief langzaam op gang komt door de specifieke Friese context, waaronder kleine kernen, veel platteland, beperkte capaciteit en beperkte middelen. Van-uit deze context willen Provinsje Fryslân en de Friese Energietafel de ontwikkeling van kennis, samenwerking, pro-jectondersteuning en zichtbaarheid rondom duurzame warmte bundelen binnen één programmatische aanpak. Hieruit is het programma Waarm Fryslân ontstaan, dat zich vooral richt op uitvoerende taken en daarbij voor een deel bouwt op kennis en capaciteit uit de markt. Het programma Waarm Fryslân is gestart in 2021 als Missy Wetterwaarmte om aquathermie in Fryslân te versnel-len, maar is in de tussentijd doorontwikkeld tot een breder programma voor de warmtetransitie in Fryslân. De scope is daarmee verbreed van uitsluitend aquathermie als oplossing naar duurzame warmte als opgave, waarbij aquathermie nadrukkelijk een belangrijke kans blijft, maar niet langer de enige oplossingsrichting en focus is. De opdrachtnemer wordt gevraagd om die uitvoeringskracht te leveren die er in de regio nu te weinig is. Niet door beleidsdocumenten en uitgebreide onderzoeken te produceren, maar door acties uit te voeren die direct effect hebben op de omgeving.

title: Norway – Transport services (excl. Waste transport) – International Shipping and Customs Clearance Services
description: The procurement covers the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' and the Norwegian foreign missions' requirements for international shipping services, including customs clearance services. The services comprise collection and express delivery of consignments between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' headquarters (MFA) and the foreign missions. The MFA dispatches one or more consignments daily. The supplier shall therefore collect consignments from the MFA at a fixed time once per day, and more frequently if agreed. In addition, there will be weekly shipments from the foreign missions to the MFA. These shipments shall be arranged upon request, with the respective foreign mission acting as the ordering party. The framework agreement primarily covers shipments weighing up to 300 kg. The consignments include, but are not limited to, regular mail such as letters and parcels sent between the MFA and the foreign missions, as well as goods purchased by the foreign missions from Norwegian suppliers located in and around Oslo (for example ICT equipment, furniture, lighting, office supplies and similar items). Such goods will normally be collected from the MFA; however, in exceptional cases, the supplier may be required to collect the goods directly from the relevant supplier's premises. The supplier shall perform the necessary customs formalities, including import and export declarations, related document handling, advance notifications to the importing country's authorities, and advance payment of customs duties and taxes where applicable. Shipments are generally transported as Diplomatic Pouch (diplomatic consignments), meaning that customs duties and VAT will only exceptionally apply. The supplier must therefore be able to carry out simplified customs clearance procedures for diplomatic mail and cargo, including exemptions from customs duties and taxes where such arrangements are available. The framework agreement does not cover third-country shipments, i.e. shipments between two foreign missions. The framework agreement shall have an initial term of two (2) years, with options for extension for an additional one (1) year plus one (1) year. The estimated annual value of the services covered by this procurement is NOK 5 million. The maximum value of the framework agreement for the entire contract period is NOK 32 million.

title: Denmark – Business services: law, marketing, consulting, recruitment, printing and security – Udbud af rammeaftale om vikarydelser og Try & Hire
description: Udbuddet omfatter én samlet rammeaftale vedrørende vikarydelser og Try & Hire. Formålet med udbuddet er at sikre AffaldPlus adgang til kvalificerede vikarer, som efter behov kan indgå i AffaldPlus' drift og øvrige relevante funktioner. Ydelserne skal leveres i overensstemmelse med de krav til blandt andet kompetencer, erfaring, tilgængelighed, bestilling, levering og øvrige forhold, der fremgår af kravspecifikationen og det øvrige udbudsmateriale. Try & Hire indebærer, at AffaldPlus efter nærmere angivne vilkår kan tilbydes mulighed for at fastansætte en vikar, som i en periode har været stillet til rådighed af leverandøren. De nærmere betingelser herfor fremgår af kravspecifikationen og kontrakten. Det konkrete indkøb omfatter de ydelser og tilknyttede leverancer, der fremgår af kravspecifikationen, tilbudslisten og de øvrige udbudsbilag. Kravspecifikationen indeholder de krav, som leverandøren skal opfylde i forbindelse med kontraktens gennemførelse. Ydelserne skal leveres efter AffaldPlus' konkrete og løbende behov. AffaldPlus er således ikke forpligtet til at aftage et bestemt antal vikartimer, et bestemt antal vikarer eller ydelser for et bestemt beløb, medmindre andet udtrykkeligt fremgår af udbudsmaterialet. Den anslåede værdi af rammeaftalen for den samlede løbetid udgør DKK 8.000.000 ekskl. moms. Den anslåede værdi er fastsat på baggrund af AffaldPlus' historiske forbrug, forventede fremtidige behov og øvrige relevante driftsmæssige forhold. Rammeaftalens maksimale værdi udgør DKK 10.500.000 ekskl. moms. Den maksimale værdi udgør det samlede loft for indkøb under rammeaftalen. Den anslåede værdi er ikke en garanti for et bestemt forbrug eller en bestemt omsætning. Det faktiske forbrug kan være både lavere og højere end den anslåede værdi, men kan ikke overstige rammeaftalens maksimale værdi, medmindre en ændring kan gennemføres lovligt efter de udbudsretlige regler om kontraktændringer.

title: 2027-2029 Maintenance Dredging, Anchorage Harbor, Alaska
description: THIS IS A PRESOLICITATION NOTICE ONLY FOR 2027-2029 MAINTENANCE DREDGING, ANCHORAGE HARBOR, ALASKA. OFFER OR BIDS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED FOR THIS NOTICE. This solicitation will be an Unrestricted Procurement. Any resulting contract will be firm-fixed priced. The solicitation for this project will be available by INTERNET ACCESS ONLY and the anticipated download availability date for this solicitation will be on or after 27 October 2026. Access to the documents will be through a link on the SAM.gov website (http://www.SAM.gov). Use the Search function and use this solicitation number to Search by Solicitation/Award Number. Any future amendments to the solicitation will also be available for download from the link shared on the SAM.gov website. The Contractor shall comply with commercial and industry standards as well as all applicable Federal, State, and local laws, regulations, and procedures. The Construction Wage Rates (formerly Davis-Bacon Act) will apply. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code will be 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, which has a size standard of $37 Million. The total estimated magnitude of construction for base and option items is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. The type of contract shall be firm-fixed price. The estimated award date of this contract is January 2027. This project is contingent on availability of funds. If the project is cancelled, all proposal preparation costs will be borne by the offeror. All offerors are advised that they must be registered in SAM.gov (http://www.sam.gov) when submitting an offer or quotation and at time of award. Joint ventures must also be registered in SAM.gov as a joint venture. Offerors who are not registered in SAM.gov should consider applying for registration immediately. See (https://ww.sam.gov) for information on registration. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: Perform surveying, dredging and disposal of approximately 900,000 cubic yards of fine-grained shoaled material annually for three (3) years at the Anchorage Harbor with an option to annually dredge 350,000 cubic yards of sandy material with some cobbles in Cook Inlet Navigation Channel. The dredging must be accomplished in a manner that keeps the Port of Alaska dock face and terminals accessible for shipping traffic at all times. The Cook Inlet Navigation Channel, which is the marked entrance through Knik Arm Shoal to Anchorage Harbor, may also require periodic maintenance dredging. The Contractor is to furnish all labor, equipment, supplies, materials, supervision and other items and services necessary to accomplish the work. All maintenance dredging in Anchorage Harbor and Cook Inlet Navigation Channel shall be performed using hopper or mechanical dredges only. Cutterhead, suction and pipeline dredges are not permissible. The type of contract shall be firm-fixed price. Construction wage rates (formerly Davis-Bacon Act wage rates) shall apply. Search via Solicitation Number Search W911KB27RA002. Additional information concerning PIEE can be found at: https://pieetraining.eb.mil/wbt/xhtml/wbt/sol/index.xhtml
